name: pin-barrel
title: Pin Barrel
description: A cron-expression field with a physical firing preview: five mono sub-inputs sit above a seven-day rule of muted dots, and every hour the expression actually fires gets a raised pin that seats with a small spring overshoot and drops out when the expression changes.
useWhen: authoring or sanity-checking a cron RECURRENCE EXPRESSION and needing the 'does */2 mean every two hours' question answered by seeing the concrete firings fall out of the five fields as you type, real crontab syntax kept intact. schedule-ascii-freebusy is the pick instead when the job is reading a group's pre-existing free/busy calendars to find an open meeting slot — it has no editable recurrence rule and no crontab syntax at all, only read-only attendee availability.
instruction: Build <PinBarrel defaultValue onChange label className> as a pure DOM+CSS cron-expression editor (no canvas, no WebGL). FIELDS: a <fieldset><legend> holding five real <input data-field="minute|hour|dom|month|dow"> cells in crontab order, each a plain-text mono field (no native number stepper) with a visually-hidden <label> for its accessible name and aria-describedby pointing at one shared plain-language sentence. Each field is parsed independently — tokens '*', 'a', 'a,b,c', 'a-b', '*/n', 'a-b/n' — and a field whose value fails to parse gets aria-invalid plus its own inline dashed border-bottom (var(--foreground), never a color-only or --error cue) without blocking the other four; ANY invalid field empties the whole barrel of pins (parsed=null short-circuits the firing computation) while leaving the rest of the UI live. The field currently focused prints its full role name ('minute', 'day of month', ...) in text-ns-muted directly beneath that one input, fading in/out over 150ms; unfocused fields show nothing there so the row reads like a real crontab line, not a labeled form. PLAIN LANGUAGE + LIVE REGION: one aria-live=polite region (referenced by every field's aria-describedby) renders a generated sentence — 'At minute 0 past every 2nd hour' for '0 */2 * * *' — built per-field ('every 2nd hour' for */2, 'minute 0' for a bare number, 'minutes 1, 15' for a list, 'hours 9 through 17' for a range, month/day-of-week numbers rendered as names) plus a second line 'next run: Tue 14:00' computed by an independent minute-by-minute forward scan from now (real cron day semantics: day-of-month OR day-of-week when BOTH are restricted from '*', otherwise whichever one is restricted). THE BARREL: an aria-hidden, overflow-x-auto strip of 168 inline mono cells (24h x 7 days, anchored to local midnight) rendered as a single flow of glyphs — '·' at rest, '┊' every 24th cell marking a day boundary, and '╹' replacing either glyph on any hour where hour+month+day match (the representative firing shown on hover is the smallest value in the parsed minute set, with a '+N more that hour' suffix when the minute field yields more than one). A '▏' read-head is absolutely positioned at the real current-time fraction of the 168-hour window and is re-targeted every 30s with a matching 30s linear CSS transition, so it creeps continuously in real time at zero rAF cost — no per-frame loop anywhere in the component. MOTION (the physical part): changing any field diffs the new set of matching hour-cells against what's currently rendered, keyed by hour-cell index. Newly-matching cells mount pre-transition (translateY(4px) scale(0.4) opacity 0, transition:none), then a doubled requestAnimationFrame flips a single `armed` flag that transitions every entering pin to its resting transform over 220ms on the back-out bezier cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1) — a small mechanical overshoot, the same technique counter-carry-ripple's column reveals use, with no spring differential-equation loop required. Cells that stop matching keep rendering for 120ms with a plain translateY(6px)+fade-out on cubic-bezier(0.55,0,1,0.45) before their node is dropped, so departure reads as a drop, not a disappearance; cells whose match status is unchanged never replay any animation, even when the representative minute they show updates. Hovering a pin sets a fixed-position detail line beneath the barrel (crossfading 150ms opacity against the resting hint, exactly schedule-ascii-freebusy's hover-line idiom) printing that firing's full absolute timestamp ('Tue 16 Aug, 14:00') — nothing ever floats over the rule itself. prefers-reduced-motion collapses straight to the resting frame for every cell (no enter/exit choreography played) and the read-head's creep transition is dropped to `none` so it just snaps to the correct position on each 30s tick — always usable, never stuck mid-animation. A11Y (the real surface, since the barrel above is aria-hidden): the sentence + next-run live region is the assistive-tech-facing equivalent of the whole rule, and a <button aria-expanded aria-controls data-firings-toggle> disclosure reveals a plain <ul> where every matching hour is a <li data-firing-item> with its full timestamp — the individual-firings list the pin rule encodes for anyone who cannot hover a pin. COLOR: token-only (--background --foreground --ns-muted --border --ns-accent through Tailwind utilities, arbitrary-opacity tints like text-ns-muted/40, and one `var(--foreground)` inline for the invalid-field underline) — --ns-accent appears only on focus-visible rings and on a hovered pin, never as resting decoration or the read-head, which is plain text-foreground. Every input and the disclosure button carries a visible focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ns-accent ring (outline-none paired only with focus-visible:ring, never with focus-visible:outline-*, so the ring is never suppressed by --tw-outline-style:none).
